method: initialize + tools/list (anonymous, no tool called; roadmap#992)

tools.description:
Search the public Anjuna docs index.

Args:
    query: Plain-text search string (same idea as the site's search box)—keywords, commands, or short
        phrases. No boolean or field-specific query language is exposed; refine with ``build``,
        ``version``, ``limit``, and alternate wording if needed.
    limit: Maximum number of hits (1–50). Omit or 0 for the server default.
    build: Product filter: nitro, sev, k8s-sev, sgx, or apm. On most deployments this is
        **required**: if you omit it, the response has ``build_required`` and ``build_options`` instead
        of ``hits`` so you can retry with the right product. (Some servers are configured to allow
        unscoped search without ``build``.)
    version: Optional doc version (e.g. v1.56). If empty, and ``build`` is set,
        the server resolves the current published version from the on-disk tech stub
        (same as /latest/{build}/) and filters to that version. If the stub is unavailable,
        only tier and optional product filters apply.

Returns:
    JSON string. On success: ok, hits (snippets + url + url_absolute + resource_uri for read_resource),
    fetch_urls, estimatedTotalHits, optional applied_version_filter. Use read_resource(resource_uri) for full
    page text when needed. If ``build`` was required but empty: build_required, build_options, empty hits.
    Or error.
tools.name: search_docs

tools.description:
Return one public documentation page as plain text (from a search_docs hit).

Use the **site-relative** ``url`` field returned by ``search_docs`` (starts with ``/latest/``).
This is equivalent to reading the ``anjuna://docs/html/...`` resource but works in clients that
only list tools. Origin follows the same rules as ``url_absolute`` in search (request Host when allowed,
else env / default).

Args:
    url: Site-relative path, e.g. ``/latest/nitro/v1.56/getting_started/foo.html``.

Returns:
    JSON string: ``ok``, ``url``, ``url_absolute``, and ``text`` on success; or ``ok: false`` and ``error``.
tools.name: get_doc_page
